newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill yields seen rising next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill yields seen rising next week.

text.p: Polish T-bill yields are expected to rise at Tuesday's one billion zloty primary tender after comparable NBP-bill yields increased by 15 basis points this week, dealers said on Friday.

Last Tuesday the National Bank of Poland increased the average yield of its 91-day NBP-bills, which are only available to Polish banks, to 22.15 percent and dealers said treasury bill yields should follow suit.
"After NBP-bill yields increased T-bill yields should rise next week, especially for the shortest 13-week paper," said Piotr Bednarek, senior debt dealer from ING Bank in Warsaw.

Dealers said it was not clear whether demand at the auction would match the treasury's offer after bids dwindled to 632 million at this week's 1.2 billion zloty auction as banks were short of cash at the end of the financial month.

"It remains to be seen how quickly one-day rates fall during the new monthly reserve period and how much spare cash banks will have to gamble for higher yields," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
Dealers expected the benchmark 52-week T-bill average yield rising to as high as 21.55 percent from 21.43 this week.
They said the average yield of the 26-week paper should rise to about 21.60 percent from 21.49 and the 13-week yield to about 21.65 percent from 21.39 percent.

Dealers said foreign investors, who over the last several weeks had been subdued by a stale near-term interest rate outlook and no zloty devaluation rate cut prospects, were likely to only place small amounts of bids on Tuesday.
The money market was expected to open the April reserve on Tuesday with one-day rates above 23 percent, down from this week's close around the 25-percent lombard rate, dealers said.

They said that because banks were likely to start April with low average reserve levels one-day rates would likely remain above the main central bank reverse repo rate, at 22.15 percent for 14-days, until at least the end of next week.
The zloty was expected to drift sideways without much impetus next week as foreign investors were not expected to play a large role at next week's treasury auctions.

"It is likely to remain between 2.8 and 3.1 percent from the parity rate next week, with a strong resistance barrier and NBP intervention level in the region of 3.2 percent," said Mateusz Bieniek, forex dealer at Societe Generale in Warsaw.
On Friday the zloty traded around 2.90 percent from the trading band centre, slightly softer than last week's close at 2.99 percent from parity.
